title: 3Sum Closest
prompt: Given an integer array `nums` of length `n` and an integer `target`, find three integers in `nums` such that the sum is closest to `target`. Return the sum of those three integers. You may assume each input has exactly one solution.

examples.explanation: The sum -1 + 2 + 1 = 2 is closest to target 1.

hints: Checking every triplet directly is O(n^3). Sorting first opens the door to a faster approach, just like the exact-sum version of this problem.
Fix one number and use two pointers over the rest of the sorted array to search for the pair that gets you closest to the remaining target.

Track the best (closest) sum found across all fixed choices; when the two-pointer sum is too low move the low pointer up, too high move the high pointer down, and if you ever hit target exactly you can return immediately.

solution.approach: Sort the array, then for each index i, run a two-pointer scan over the rest of the array to find the pair whose sum plus nums[i] is closest to target. If the running sum is less than target, move the low pointer right to increase it; if greater, move the high pointer left to decrease it; update the closest-sum-seen at every step. This mirrors the 3Sum two-pointer structure but tracks distance-to-target instead of an exact zero match, giving O(n^2) instead of the O(n^3) brute force.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra space, excluding sort space
